etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Inherited from Middle English table, tabel, tabil, tabul, from Old English tabele, tabul, tablu, tabule, tabula (“board”); also as tæfl, tæfel, an early Germanic borrowing of Latin tabula (“tablet, board, plank, chart”). The sense of “piece of furniture” is from Old French table, of same Latin origin; Old English used bēod or bord instead for this meaning: see board. Doublet of tabula and tavla.
senses: (countable) Furniture with a top surface to accommodate a variety of uses.
To tabulate; to put into a table or grid. [from 15th c.]
